title: KONGSBERG Canada accelerates space & defence industrial expansion in Canada with strategic agreements with MDA Space and Telesat | Telesat
body_markdown:
*Announcements coincide with the official visit of Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre to Ottawa, advancing Canada–Norway’s defence and security partnership, and will bolster sovereign industrial capabilities from deep sea to space.*


**OTTAWA, ONTARIO – September 21, 2026 –** KONGSBERG Canada today announced an expansion of its Canadian industrial presence across the space and defence sectors, marked by the execution of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with MDA Space Ltd. and a strategic Letter of Intent (LOI) with Telesat LEO ULC, a subsidiary of Telesat Corporation (Nasdaq and TSX: TSAT). These agreements coincide with the official visit of Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre to Ottawa, reflecting the deepening strategic alliance between Canada and Norway following the bilateral Strategic Cooperation Agreement signed earlier this year.


Under these strategic agreements, KONGSBERG is establishing dedicated partnerships with premier Canadian space leaders to strengthen technical cooperation and sovereign communications.


- **MOU with MDA Space Ltd.:** Establishes a collaborative framework between KONGSBERG and MDA Space Ltd. to explore joint space and defence projects and technical cooperation in a variety of domains.


- **LOI with Telesat LEO ULC** : Establishes a strategic intent to leverage and evaluate the integration of the Telesat Lightspeed low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network into KONGSBERG defence platforms and solution architectures. This cooperation would support the delivery of secure, resilient, low-latency military connectivity for Norway, Canada and their allies.


As founding NATO allies and fellow Arctic Council nations, Canada and Norway share an enduring commitment to democracy, the rule of law, and the collective security of the High North. As Canada accelerates defence spending to rearm and reinforce the Canadian Armed Forces, KONGSBERG brings over a century of extreme-environment innovation and 50 years of operational presence in Canada to support national security priorities.


“Signing this MOU today responds to the strategic partnership between Norway and Canada announced in March. KONGSBERG is already present in Canada, and we look forward to strengthening our collaboration.”
— Camilla Kiss, President, Kongsberg Discovery and Executive Vice President, KONGSBERG


“KONGSBERG’s work in Ottawa directly strengthens the security, sovereignty, and readiness of both Canada and Norway. These new agreements with Canada’s two premiere space companies reinforce our commitment to supporting Canada’s defence and security industries across every operational domain—from deep sea to outer space.”
— Jordan Freed, President, Kongsberg Geospatial


“This MOU is a reflection of the immediate opportunities for global industry leaders to work together to meet the defence and security needs of trusted partners and allies. We look forward to working with Kongsberg to ensure that military and security forces have the space and defence capabilities needed for their mission critical work.”
— Mike Greenley, CEO, MDA Space


“This collaboration reflects the strength of the Canada-Norway strategic relationship and our shared commitment to advancing sovereign and allied defence capabilities. The combination of KONGSBERG’s advanced defence platforms and systems with the secure, resilient and low-latency capabilities of the Telesat Lightspeed network would create the opportunity to enhance mission-critical communications and deliver greater operational effectiveness for Norway, Canada and allied nations.”
— Dan Goldberg, President and CEO, Telesat
